beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: What appears as a model can include suffering they cannot safely dismiss.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The novel brings human experience into contact with the children's incomplete understanding.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Elias offers one important human perspective inside that larger arrangement.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: His presence complicates the separation between studying someone and owing them something.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The story's different scales keep that encounter morally unstable.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The children call the system's reward yield, and they need it.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: That dependence makes observation and intervention difficult to separate from appetite.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: A result can become attractive because it keeps the observer alive.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The novel asks how judgment changes under such conditions.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Its danger does not require a child to begin with cruel intentions.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Fear, ignorance, and dependence can already distort the meaning of help.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Reading the scenes reveals those pressures before any simple moral classification fits.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The children also try to make a home together.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: They need company, familiar rhythms, and moments that do not serve measurement.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: The book gives those needs space beside its more disturbing experiments.

beats.speaker: narrator
beats.text: Borrowed parental voices raise questions about comfort, ownership, and another person's life.
